classification.difficultyReason: Cosine rule for the angle, then parallelogram area as twice the triangle.

content.prompt:
A parallelogram $PQRS$ has sides $PQ=SR=14\text{ cm}$ and $QR=PS=9\text{ cm}$.
The diagonal $PR$ is $12\text{ cm}$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use the cosine rule to find the size of $\angle PQR$, correct to the nearest degree.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence find the area of the parallelogram, correct to the nearest cm$^2$.

answer.worked:
The diagonal $PR$ splits the parallelogram into two congruent triangles. Using the unrounded angle,
$$\begin{align*}A&=2\times\frac12(14)(9)\sin\angle PQR\\A&=126\sin\!\left(\cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac{19}{36}\right)\right)\\A&=\frac72\sqrt{935}\text{ cm}^2\\A&\approx107\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
